tagline: A flat river plain with a giant Buddha, old temples, craft villages, and life along the Chao Phraya
introHtml:
Ang Thong is a small central-Thailand province sitting between the Chao Phraya and the Noi rivers. Most people picture the huge golden Buddha at Wat Muang that you can spot from far off, plus the cluster of old temples scattered along the water. The town is close to Ayutthaya and Bangkok, so you can drive in for the day and head back by evening, or tack it onto an Ayutthaya trip over two days.

Beyond the temples, Ang Thong has craft villages that have been at it for generations — the drum-making village at Ban Ekkarat and the village that sculpts court-style dolls. In between you get rice fields and riverside orchards. It's an unhurried province where you can pay respects at the temples, watch the craftspeople work, and grab local roadside food without any fuss.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable — you can do temples and drive along the river all day without the heat

highlights.name: Wat Muang (the giant Buddha)
highlights.blurb: Home to Phra Phuttha Maha Nawamin, a huge golden Buddha visible from a distance. It's the image people associate with Ang Thong and the one stop nobody skips.

highlights.name: Wat Khun Inthapramun (the long reclining Buddha)
highlights.blurb: An old temple with a long open-air reclining Buddha, one of the longest in Thailand. The grounds are wide, open, and shaded.

highlights.name: Ban Ekkarat drum-making village
highlights.blurb: A village that has made and sold drums for generations. Drums of all sizes line the roadside to look at and buy — a craft the province is known for.

highlights.name: Ban Bang Sadet court-doll village
highlights.blurb: A riverside community that sculpts clay dolls depicting Thai life. There's a center where you can watch the sculpting and buy pieces to take home.

highlights.name: Wat Pa Mok Worawihan
highlights.blurb: A Chao Phraya riverside temple with an old reclining Buddha in the hall. Legend says it once floated down the river — a temple long tied to the town by the water.

highlights.name: Life along the Chao Phraya and Noi rivers
highlights.blurb: Ang Thong is a flat plain on both banks. Drive along the water past temples, rice fields, and orchards, and you see everyday village life kept simple.

foodScene.name: Boat noodles (kuai tiao ruea)
foodScene.note: Ang Thong sits in central Thailand's boat-noodle belt — small bowls with a strong, dark broth that you order several at a time at roadside shops.

foodScene.name: River fish and river prawns
foodScene.note: A Chao Phraya town has fresh freshwater fish and river prawns — grilled fish, tom yum, and grilled prawns at the riverside places.

foodScene.name: Khanom keson lamchiak
foodScene.note: A local Ang Thong sweet — thin pastry sheets wrapped around sweet coconut filling. It's an old souvenir treat you'll find around Pa Mok.

foodScene.name: Thai sweets and local souvenirs
foodScene.note: Markets and shops in town carry homestyle Thai sweets and local souvenirs to take back.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are everywhere in town and along the road — bold flavors that suit travelers.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with plenty of places to choose from — relaxed vibe and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Beef noodles and made-to-order dishes
foodScene.note: In town there are long-running beef-noodle shops and made-to-order places — an easy meal at local prices.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and by the river
foodScene.note: Small cafes in town and along the river make a good spot to rest over coffee after the temples.

attractions.name: Wat Muang
attractions.blurb: The temple with the huge golden Buddha you can see from afar. Around the grounds there are statues and a heaven-and-hell garden to walk through — the main draw for anyone visiting Ang Thong.

attractions.name: Wat Khun Inthapramun
attractions.blurb: An old temple with a long open-air reclining Buddha, one of the longest in Thailand, set on a wide, shaded ground.

attractions.name: Wat Pa Mok Worawihan
attractions.blurb: A Chao Phraya riverside temple with an old reclining Buddha in the hall. The setting is calm by the water, with a floating-Buddha legend told alongside it.

attractions.name: Ban Ekkarat drum-making village
attractions.blurb: A craft village that has made drums for generations. Drums of all sizes line the roadside — stop to watch the making and buy one as a souvenir.

attractions.name: Ban Bang Sadet court-doll village
attractions.blurb: A riverside community that sculpts clay dolls depicting Thai life, with a center where you can watch the sculpting and pick pieces to take home.

attractions.name: Wat Ton Son
attractions.blurb: A temple in town with a large metal-cast Buddha in the subduing-Mara pose — an important temple that locals come to pay respects at.

attractions.name: San Chao Rong Thong market, Wiset Chai Chan
attractions.blurb: An old, still-busy market on the Noi River with local food and souvenirs — a pleasant place to wander and watch local life.

attractions.name: Rice fields and the Chao Phraya riverside
attractions.blurb: The flat plain on both banks is full of rice fields and orchards. Driving or cycling along the water to take in village life is easy going.

itineraryIdeas: Ang Thong — Wat Muang and Wat Khun Inthapramun temples in a day
